images.text:
Bianca: Hey, I just finished work. I saw your text. What's up?
Kristi: I decided that I should apply to this position. When will I ever get another chance like this?
Bianca: Awesome, but you will have to apply before it's too late. You won't be able to apply if the deadline passes.
Kristi: Really? Even if it's an internal posting?
Bianca: Of course, they still have a cut-off date for those.
Kristi: I will be sending in my application after I gather all the required documents.

Bianca: What do you need?
Kristi: I'll have to provide them with an updated résumé, a completed internal application form and I'm guessing something that's similar to a cover letter.
Bianca: I think you mean a letter of intent.
Kristi: Right. After getting this job and doing all this reading, I've forgotten what all these different documents are. What is that again?
Bianca: It's very similar to a cover letter. The only difference is that you mention your intentions.
Kristi: Okay. While writing this letter, what should I make sure to include?

Bianca: When crafting a letter of intent, emphasize your qualifications and your interest in learning more about the company. It's also important to remind the reader about any accomplishments you have achieved while working with the company.
Kristi: I will have you look at my letter before I send it to the recruitment officer.
Bianca: Of course. I'll look at it when I get home. Will you be done by then?
Kristi: Only if I start right now ... talk to you later!
Bianca: Bye!

Clauses Using -ing After Since and Ever
After since, after, before, while, when and whenever, an -ING form in the verb is needed.

For example:

Since reading the book, I've refused to read any other author.
After waiting for ages in line, we decided to go to another pub.

Future Continuous and Future Perfect: Will in Time and If-Clauses

Use the future continuous when you talk about future actions that will be happening at a certain time in the future. </br>Use the Future Perfect when you talk about an action that will be finished by a certain time in the future.

Future Continuous is used to:

  • discuss an action that will be in progress at a specific time in the future.
Example:
This time tomorrow, I will be flying to New York.

  • predict or guess future events.
Example:
We expect she will be coming to the presentation.

  • refer to repetitive events that are expected to happen in the future.
Example:
I will be talking to my boss for the whole week. We are taking a trip together.

The structure of Future Continuous is:
subject + will + be + v-ing
Example:
I'll be reading this book until the end of the week.

Future Perfect is used to discuss an action that will be completed by a specific time in the future.
Example:
I will have finished this book by the end of the week.
By the end of 2030 scientists will have discovered the cure for many diseases.

The structure of Future Perfect is:
Future Perfect subject + will + have + past participle
Example:
I will have finished this report by the end of the month.

You can use time clauses beginning with when, as soon as, until, before etc. with the Future Continuous.
Example:
I will not be talking to her until she says sorry.

With conditional clauses, we can use will only when we want emphasis - it makes an intention or promise stronger.
Example:
If you will insist on coming with us, then you must expect to pay your own way.
I will have finished it by the time you get home.
I'll be starting on that when we end this call.
